text: Shaun Gallagher's 'interaction theory' of social cognition claims that in most everyday encounters we understand others:
choices: By directly perceiving their mental states in embodied expression and interaction, prior to theory or simulation
By applying a tacit folk-psychological theory of mind
By running an offline simulation of their perspective
By analogical inference from our own single case
explanation: Interaction theory (Gallagher, with Zahavi) holds that social understanding is primarily direct, embodied perception of others in expression and interaction, more basic than either theorizing or simulating. Applying a tacit theory is theory-theory; offline simulation is simulation theory; analogical inference is the classical argument from analogy — the three approaches interaction theory rejects as primary.
